title: What Startup Playbook Is and Why It Matters
summary: The foundations of startup playbook: what it is and why getting it right pays off.
body:
Startups: find a painful problem, build the smallest solution, get 10 customers who love it, then scale. Most startups die from building what nobody wants.

Why it matters: #1 startup killer: no market need Talk to 100+ users before scaling

This guide walks the full ladder — foundations first, then compounded practice, then advanced mastery. Every record is actionable: read in order, do the steps, run the numbers.

title: Getting Started: Your First Five Moves in Startup Playbook
summary: Start startup playbook this week with five concrete moves.
body:
Don't try to do everything. Do these five, in order:

1. Find a painful, frequent problem
2. Interview 50-100 potential users
3. Build the smallest viable product
4. Get 10 delighted users
5. Charge from day one (even a little)

Five moves, one week. Momentum beats perfection — the rest of this guide builds on exactly this start.
facts: Charge from day one (even a little)

title: Startup Playbook Beginner FAQ
summary: Straight answers to the most common startup playbook questions.
body:
Q: Raise money?
A: Only when you have traction; revenue first.

Q: Cofounder?
A: Yes if skill gaps demand it; vest everything.

Q: When to pivot?
A: When users consistently want something adjacent.

Still stuck? Start with record 2 of this guide and do the first move today.

title: Startup Playbook: Safety, Legal, and Fine Print
summary: What to watch out for with startup playbook: safety, contracts, and fine print.
body:
Read before you act: Stealth mode (nobody cares yet) And: Building for a year without users

General rules: get agreements in writing, understand what you're signing, keep records of money in and out, and know when a professional (lawyer, accountant, vet, doctor — depending on the domain) is worth the fee. An hour of professional advice beats a month of fixing.

title: Doing Startup Playbook With Others: Family and Team Edition
summary: Startup Playbook as a team sport: dividing roles and keeping everyone aligned.
body: Startup Playbook multiplies with help: assign roles from the steps (find a painful, frequent problem to one person, build the smallest viable product to another), agree on the numbers (#1 startup killer: no market need), and hold a 15-minute weekly check-in. Write down who owns what — teams fail on ambiguity, not effort.

body: Quarterly: review the numbers (Talk to 100+ users before scaling) and re-run the plan. Yearly: hire slowly; fire fast and a full reset of tools and checklists. Annual rhythms beat annual panics — put the reviews on the calendar now.
